standard_prerequisites.name: Infinitary Scott analysis and back-and-forth preservation
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Sigma-in_alpha formula is an infinitary countable disjunction of existential blocks over lower-level Pi formulas, with the dual definition for Pi. The back-and-forth preorder matches those formula classes. If all tuple orbits are Sigma-in_alpha definable over a fixed finite tuple, a Sigma-in_(alpha+2) Scott sentence exists. A nonisomorphic K with L<=_beta K rules out a Pi-in_beta Scott sentence of L.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Source45-86 and the stated standard background173-184.
standard_prerequisites.use: Translate the actual orbit upper bounds and constructed nonisomorphic back-and-forth witness into exact sentence complexity.

standard_prerequisites.name: Classical Scott analysis of well orders and finite condensation
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a nonzero countable limit ordinal lambda, omega^lambda <=_(lambda+1) omega^lambda*2. For each gamma<omega^lambda its interval isomorphism type has infinitary complexity below lambda. The finite-condensation relations start with equality, take finite distance in the quotient at successors, and take unions at limits; relation sim_delta is Sigma-in_(2*delta) definable.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Source1314-1333,1381-1391 and1530-1544; Ash1986, Ash-Knight2000 and Alvir-Rossegger2020.
standard_prerequisites.use: Only the well-order building blocks and definability of block relations are allowed. The shuffle-sum construction, orbit definitions and two-round back-and-forth argument are not assumed.

core_obligations: Prove the shuffle-sum lemma that inserting a distinguished L block costs two rounds in the asymmetric back-and-forth comparison.
Construct the two dense sums with blocks 1+Z+omega^lambda and 1+Z+omega^lambda*2, then insert one distinguished block at their interface.
Define singleton finite blocks, Z positions, first ordinal positions and second ordinal positions by the displayed infinitary formulas, with the required quantifier-complexity bounds.
Recover tuple orbits over the distinguished interface point and prove the upper Scott-sentence bound.
Use the two-round lemma and a genuinely nonisomorphic order obtained by removing the first doubled block to prove no Pi-in_(lambda+3) Scott sentence exists.

proof_roadmap.step: Two-stage interval strategy: first copy the initial and terminal shuffle sums, then absorb the distinguished block into a final segment; reduce the only nonisomorphic interval to the given alpha-comparison.
Construct L1,L2,A,B,L and define orbits in the one-ordinal blocks.
Define second-copy initial points using all lower finite-condensation relations, then all remaining positions with one additional alternation.
Apply the fully supplied shuffle lemma for the matching lower bound.

difficulty_reason: Even after standard Scott analysis of well orders is allowed, the task must combine a bespoke two-round shuffle-sum comparison with an explicit transfinite orbit-definability construction. The upper and lower bounds involve different mechanisms: locating the second omega^lambda copy by all lower condensation relations, and concealing an inserted distinguished block from a long back-and-forth game. It is not just calculating the rank of a given ordinal. The precise H2/H3 boundary remains for independent review.

compared.difference: The public primary is the back-and-forth behavior of powers of Z. This target is a dense mixed-block order of exact Sigma-in_(lambda+3) complexity; its proof does not use the published timesZ lemma.

editorial_notes: All ordinals in this Scott-analysis problem are countable, and limit ordinal means nonzero limit. L times Q replaces each rational point with a copy of L, as defined in1017-1020.

The author proof at1556 calls z the second-copy initial element, while the displayed sec(x,z) formula and its subsequent use1557 specify x as that element and z as the initial element of the first copy. The formula is preserved; this variable-description slip is explicitly recorded for independent review.

The upper-bound passage uses the standard named-parameter Scott-rank criterion stated among the inputs. The lower-bound comparison is with A+B; it is not isomorphic to A+L2+B because the latter has a least doubled-ordinal block and the former does not.

review_checkpoints: The two-round lemma keeps fixed initial/final fragments and reduces the central nonisomorphic interval to the assumed alpha-comparison, not to an unjustified isomorphism.

The sec(x,z) formula selects the first point of the second omega^lambda copy: the no-intervening-singleton condition keeps it in the same block, and all lower condensation relations fail across the lambda-cut.

Tuple orbit descriptions also include relative order, shared macroblocks and finite successor distances in Z, as in the author earlier tuple argument1073-1075; these are routine definable relations, not a new classification theorem.
The nonisomorphism needed by the lower-bound corollary is witnessed by whether a first doubled-ordinal block exists.
